case_name: Amanda Renee Stewart v. Commissioner (Ahmed Zied, Intervenor)

taxpayer.notes: Petitioner (requesting spouse) and intervenor married 2016, legally separated August 2019, marriage dissolved June 15, 2020 (final six months later). Unreported income solely intervenor's consulting business.

adjustments: unreported taxable wages and nonemployee compensation
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Petitioner raised only the affirmative defense of relief from joint and several liability under sec. 6015(c); did not contest the deficiency
conceded: IRS/respondent conceded petitioner is entitled to sec. 6015(c) relief for the portion of the deficiency and penalty attributable to intervenor's unreported business income

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner and intervenor married in 2016 and divorced in 2020; lived in California
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner, Amanda Renee Stewart, and intervenor, Ahmed Zied, were married in 2016 and divorced in 2020.
they were legally separated in August 2019.

findings_of_fact.fact: Joint 2019 return filed electronically via TurboTax; intervenor entered his own business information
findings_of_fact.snippet: petitioner was under the impression that the former couple was required to jointly file their 2019 Form 1040

findings_of_fact.fact: Marriage dissolved June 15, 2020; divorce final six months later
findings_of_fact.snippet: The San Diego Superior Court dissolved p etitioner’s and intervenor’s marriage on June 15, 2020

findings_of_fact.fact: Notice dated January 10, 2022 determined deficiency $33,028 and sec. 6662(b)(2) penalty $6,474 from unreported wages and nonemployee compensation
Petitioner was not part of intervenor's business and had no insight into it; unaware of the omitted income
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was not a part of his business and had no insight into his business affairs.

findings_of_fact.fact: Intervenor did not file his own petition despite receiving the notice
findings_of_fact.snippet: Intervenor did not file his own petition, despite having received a copy of the Notice.

issues.question: Other (sec. 6015(c) innocent spouse relief): Do intervenor's objections (unfairness; desire to amend the return and claim offsetting deductions) defeat petitioner's entitlement to sec. 6015(c) relief for 2019?
issues.holding: No; sec. 6015(c) requirements not in dispute; fairness objection irrelevant; intervenor cannot enlarge issues or redetermine the deficiency (no timely petition); petitioner relieved for portion of deficiency and penalty attributable to intervenor's business income
issues.computable_reason: Sec. 6015(c) elements (joint return, divorced at election, timely election, unpaid deficiency) and allocation of items to intervenor follow from found facts; objections fail as a matter of law

decision.text: Decision will be entered for petitioner.
decision.summary: Petitioner granted sec. 6015(c) relief from joint and several liability for the 2019 deficiency and penalty attributable to intervenor's business income; intervenor's objections rejected

notes: Respondent conceded relief (IRS had granted 6015(c) administratively). Allocation is per sec. 6015(d)(3)(A) as if separate returns; specific allocated amounts not stated. Court lacks power to order amended returns. Note intervenor's admission in Form 12508 that business amounts were misreported.
